title: Workload Fingerprint Orchestrator and Baseline Extrapolator for Prefill/Decode Scheduling
creator: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: current CI performance gates and synthetic workloads overfit to a handful of canonical traces, which misses fractional regressions introduced by kernel routing and attention tweaks. This ticket builds an orchestrator that fingerprints incoming production traces into stable cohorts and a baseline extrapolator that synthesizes realistic variants for prefill/decode scheduling runs. Goals: 1) group traces by runtime-relevant features (sequence-length histogram, kv-cache hit pattern, attention sparsity, token-type mix); 2) create deterministic cohort seeds that are small, replayable, and representative; 3) extrapolate minimal perturbations (sequence stretch/shrink, kv-offset shifts, attention-window variance) to stress kernel selection and scheduling; 4) wire the output into our CI perf gates so regressions are caught at cohort granularity rather than only global percentiles.
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint algorithm produces stable cohort IDs for >95% of traces over 7 days of production traffic
Extrapolator can generate 50 synthetic variants for a cohort with configurable perturbation envelopes
Bench harness accepts cohort manifests and schedules prefill/decode runs across kernel candidates deterministically
CI perf gate shows cohort-level baselines and fails if median latency regresses >3% or p99 regresses >5% for any kernel on a cohort
Telemetry: cohort tags emitted in traces and bench runs; dashboard shows cohort health and diff views
steps: Design fingerprint schema and saving format (compact proto line format) — include features, hash, and seed
Implement lightweight fingerprint extractor (Go) to run as trace post-processor and in bench ingestion
Build baseline extrapolator service (Python) that accepts a seed trace and produces parameterized variants
Extend bench harness to accept cohort manifests and variant envelopes; add deterministic RNG seeding and seed-lock files
Add cohort-aware CI perf gate logic: run target kernels across cohort variants in PRs and nightly runs; compute cohort deltas and alert rules
Expose dashboards: cohort distribution, per-kernel cohort performance, regression timeline, and synthetic variant breakdown
Run backfill: process 14 days of historical traces, create cohort baselines, and validate stability metrics
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Kickoff — gathered initial requirements from serving-rt and infra. Priorities: determinism, low overhead in production, and quick CI turnaround time.

2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor: Prototype fingerprint shape: [seq_hist, kv_hit_ratio, avg_decode_len, attention_density, token_entropy]. Implemented hashing + stable bucketing. Pushed branch: github.com/redwood/bench/prototype/fingerprint (WIP).
2026-03-11 Priya Rao (review): Recommend including model_variant and quantization label in fingerprint so CI can gate per-quant profile. Also requested privacy review for trace-derived features.

2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Added quantization label and stripped any customer PII fields. Running small backfill on dev cluster (1k traces) to validate cohort stability. Initial results: 92% stable cohort assignment over 24h — need to tighten bucketing on attention_density.
2026-03-12 SRE note: Be mindful of storage of synthetic variants; set retention 14 days for generated seeds used in CI to limit costs.

2026-03-12 Design feedback (Aria Lopez): Visualizing cohorts as stacked histograms with selectable kernels would help PMs and Eng quickly identify affected buckets. Will prototype in console-ux sprint.
2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Blocking issue — current bench harness RNG seeding uses process time; switched to explicit seed-lock file approach. Need review for concurrency semantics in nightly runs.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full trace replay vs fingerprint-cohort replay. Full replay gives fidelity but is expensive and brittle; cohort extrapolation is cheaper and surfaces kernel-specific regression modes faster.
Determinism strategy: store 64-bit seed per variant and a lockfile with run metadata to make bench runs reproducible across CI agents.
Telemetry plan: add 'cohort_id' and 'variant_seed' tags to internal bench and production traces. Use existing tracing pipeline to join bench runs with prod distributions.
Rollout: feature flag the extrapolator in CI; start with nightly cohort runs, then enable PR-based cohort gating for high-risk repos (serving-rt kernels)
